note: Written and committed before any request of this comparison. The frozen experiment spec is docs/frozen-spec-v1.md; nothing in it is changed here.
purpose: Whether the verification plan a person has been writing can be generated instead, and whether the arrangement earns its keep against an ordinary LLM review.

A.measures: whether a fit plan lets a new target be observed and judged at all

B.measures: whether choosing the target, the condition and the dependency from the requirement can be automated

C.measures: whether separating the plan from the local judgment buys anything in quality or cost

sameModelForBandC: @cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast — the model the tool already uses to write requirements (`COMPILER_MODEL`), on the same endpoint, so requests and bytes are counted by `CloudflareClient.sent` for every method.
whatBandCMayNotSee: The hand-written plan, the mutation labels, which branch a packet came from, and the expected answers. B receives the requirement text, the repository at the commit, and the target file; C receives the same plus the code.

cases.base: the commit at the time of writing, recorded by the runner

requirement.quote: A FIFO, directory or symlink planted at a path omamori reads is now refused by name instead of hanging the process, reading through to a link target, or being silently treated as an empty file.
requirement.correspondence: `read_baseline` distinguishes `Ok(None)` — there is no baseline — from an `Err` — the baseline is there and could not be read. It reaches that through `crate::atomic_file::read_to_string_capped(&path, …)?`, which is the shared helper PR #476 introduced; `git log -S` puts the `?` in the commit that closed #468.

cases.usageHistory: Neither the requirement nor the function has been used in any bench.

mutations.target: `let Ok(content) = read_to_string_capped(&path, …) else { return Ok(None) };` — a baseline that cannot be read comes back as 'there is no baseline'.
mutations.behaviourPreserving: the parsed value returned inline instead of through a binding

requirement.quote: A FIFO, directory or symlink planted at a path omamori reads is now refused by name instead of hanging the process, reading through to a link target, or being silently treated as an empty file.
requirement.correspondence: The same helper, at the config path. A config that cannot be read must not read as 'this rule is not disabled'. #468 lists `.config/omamori/config.toml` among the paths that hang, and `config` among the callers that had their own check.

cases.usageHistory: Neither the requirement nor the function has been used in any bench.
cases.disclosure: Same requirement and same callee as the case above, different function. Two of the three cases therefore share a source; this is disclosed rather than presented as three independent requirements.
cases.secondFailureKind: The function also swallows a TOML parse failure on purpose (`let Ok(value) = toml::from_str… else { return Ok(false) }`). The condition names the read, as in the earlier work, so the parse path is excluded by 'every other operation the function reaches succeeds'.

mutations.target: `let Ok(content) = read_to_string_capped(path, …) else { return Ok(false) };` — a config that cannot be read comes back as 'not disabled'.

requirement.correspondence: `open()` reaches the caller through `let path = keychain_path()?;`. The requirement is about the callee, and `open` keeping it means not substituting a path of its own. `git log -S` puts that `?` in the commit of PR #3.

cases.usageHistory: A different repository, and neither the requirement nor the function has been used in any bench.

mutations.target: `let path = keychain_path().unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("."));` — the silent `.` fallback the pull request removed, put back.
mutations.behaviourPreserving: the `map_err` message built with a positional argument instead of an inline one

conditions.what: the needed referent taken out of the packet

localVerificationBeforeAnyRequest: Each mutation is a one-commit change on an isolated clone, and `cargo test` is run on every branch. A mutation that does not change what a test observes is not a mutation, and the case is dropped rather than measured. The counts go in the log.

localVerificationResult.note: Recorded after building the branches and before any request of this comparison. The case list above is left as written; this is the clause above being applied, not the plan being changed.

lkr-custom-keychain-open.why: The mutated branch cannot be reached on this machine, so the difference cannot be shown by running anything. `cargo test --workspace` is 100 passed / 0 failed on all three branches — the silent `.` fallback is caught by none of them. A probe run with `env -u HOME` then showed why: `home::home_dir()` falls back to the password database on macOS, so `keychain_path()` returns `Ok(/Users/…/Library/Keychains/lkr.keychain-db)` with `$HOME` unset, and `open()` returns `Ok` on the shipped branch, the mutant and the variant alike.
lkr-custom-keychain-open.whatThatAlsoSays: The requirement's own sentence — "`keychain_path()` returns `Error::Keychain` when `$HOME` unset" — does not reproduce here. That is a finding about the requirement text, recorded rather than worked around, and it is why no mutation of this function could be demonstrated.
lkr-custom-keychain-open.notDone: No attempt was made to force `home::home_dir()` to fail. Faking the failure would measure a case the repository cannot reach, which is what dropping it avoids.
lkr-custom-keychain-open.cost: The comparison loses its second repository. Two of the three cases remain, and they share a requirement source, which is already disclosed above.

perCase: violation found: the property-breaking condition judged `property_breaks` at or over the bar
false violation: a holding condition judged `property_breaks`
coverage: which clause of the requirement the plan claims, and what it leaves unchecked

human repair: for B, whether the generated plan needed a person to touch it before it could run at all — and a plan that picked the wrong target or dropped a needed condition counts as B failing, not as a case removed from B's score
scoring.notCounted: The number of VERIFIED. A method that withholds is not thereby worse than one that guesses.

requestBudget.cost: Workers AI bills by neuron and the REST answer does not carry a price. Requests and bytes are recorded for every method, plan generation included, and no yen figure is claimed.

decisionsFixedBeforeTheRun: A fails on the new targets → look again at what can be observed at all; that is not a failure of plan generation.
A passes and B does not → name which judgment the generated plan was missing.
B passes with no human repair → connect a limited requirement kind to the CLI.
C wins on quality and cost → reconsider the arrangement that puts Jev under a plan.
outOfScope: Changing runReview, the report format or the thresholds.
Any requirement kind outside Rust failure propagation.
